explain.name: Votes on Measure Y
explain.why: Belmont has 17,435 registered voters in the county's precinct data. It cast 11,060 ballots in Nov 2022 and 14,219 in Nov 2024, usually turning out 4 to 13% above the county rate, and 5 to 9% of Belmont ballots skip city measures. Ballot returns this fall are running ahead of 2022.

explain.name: Counted in the 8:10 PM report
explain.why: In recent San Mateo County elections the first report held about 31 to 49% of the final count (in Nov 2022 and June 2026 it covered mail received by the Friday before; the 49% is from the March 2020 primary). This year it includes mail received through Sunday, so it should hold more. In Nov 2024, mail ballots received by 5 PM the Sunday before were 53.5% of the final count.

explain.name: In-person ballots' share
explain.value: about 8.5% (±2.5) of all votes on Y
explain.why: After 8:10 PM the county adds only ballots cast in person at vote centers. They were 6.3% of the votes on Belmont's 2022 city measure and 10.6% in 2024.

explain.name: Counted by later updates
explain.value: 66% Thu Nov 5, 72% Fri, 82% Mon Nov 9, 89% Thu Nov 12, 93% Fri, 96% Mon Nov 16
explain.why: Based on the county's pace in Nov 2022, Nov 2024 and June 2026, shifted up for this year's bigger first report. Mail postmarked by Election Day counts if it arrives by Nov 10; signature fixes are due Nov 25; the county certifies Dec 3.

explain.name: In-person ballots vs early mail
explain.value: 6 points less YES (±6; 80% range: 15 less to 3 more)
explain.why: Measured against the 8:10 PM early mail, in-person ballots ran about 1 to 5 points less YES on the county's 2022 school bonds and about 16 to 17 less on its 2022 hotel taxes, including Belmont's Measure K. Peanut's 6 sits between. Across 70 county measures since 2020, in-person ballots ran about 4.5 points less YES than all mail.

explain.name: Late ballots vs early mail
explain.value: 4 points more YES (±4.5; 80% range: 3 less to 11 more, so about 1 time in 4 they run less YES than the early mail)
explain.why: All 12 paired county property-tax measures gained YES after election night (by 0.8 to 7.3 points in the final result). On the county's Nov 2022 school bonds, late ballots ran about 3 to 6 points more YES than the early mail (4.6 on average), and more in primaries. Belmont's own city taxes that weren't property taxes barely moved after election night: against the early mail, late ballots on Belmont's 2022 hotel tax ran about 2 points less YES. Peanut sits at +4 because it's unclear which kind of tax Measure Y behaves like.

explain.name: How the two groups move together
explain.why: Measures whose in-person ballots fell furthest below the early mail also had the weakest late ballots. On the county's Nov 2022 measures, the hotel taxes ran about 16 points less YES in person and 2 to 3 less in late ballots, while the school bonds ran 1 to 5 less in person but 3 to 6 more in late ballots. So an in-person slide bigger than Peanut expects also lowers what it expects from late ballots.

explain.name: Late batches vary
explain.value: about 2 points from one batch to the next
explain.why: Late batches mix Election Day drop-offs, mail arriving by Nov 10, provisional ballots and signature fixes, which can differ. By Mon, Nov 9 this matters more than anything else while YES leads; if YES trails, how many ballots are left matters more. Nothing local measures it, so it's a judgment.

explain.name: Surprises
explain.why: Big late swings are rare but real, and close San Mateo County measures have flipped during the canvass. Fat tails (a Student-t with 5 degrees of freedom) keep Peanut from claiming certainty too early.
